behavior: Crepuscular aerial insectivore; hunts flying insects at dawn and dusk with looping, erratic, batlike flight. Rests motionless by day, often lengthwise on a branch or on open ground. Males perform steep courtship dives that produce a booming sound, and migrants may gather in large flocks.
field_marks: Cryptically mottled and barred gray, brown, black, buff, and white plumage
Bold white patch across the outer primaries
Medium-long, slightly notched tail; adult males show a white band near the tip
Small, flat head with a large dark eye, tiny bill, and broad gape
Extremely short legs and a short neck
habitat: Open ground and open-canopy habitats, including grasslands, savannas, dunes, forest clearings, burns, open forest, and rocky or gravel surfaces. Forages over open areas near woods or wetlands and lays its eggs directly on bare or sparsely vegetated ground.
